tagline: The corner of Iowa the glaciers left alone.
intro: The byway zigzags 144 miles across Allamakee and Winneshiek counties, a corner of Iowa the last glaciers passed over and left untouched. The land stayed gashed and furrowed, all limestone bluffs, wooded valleys and the river bottoms of the Mississippi, the Yellow and the Upper Iowa. The road rides it up and down like a roller coaster, down to cold-water trout streams and past stone churches and pioneer cemeteries.

Near Harpers Ferry, Effigy Mounds National Monument keeps more than 200 prehistoric mounds, some of them shaped like bears and birds. In Decorah the Vesterheim museum keeps the Norwegian-American side of the story.
season: Fall, which Travel Iowa calls an especially scenic time, when the hardwood timber turns color.

moments.title: Lansing
moments.text: Joseph "Diamond Jo" Reynolds, whose name went on a whole line of steamships, built his first boat here and named it for the town.

moments.title: Waukon
moments.text: Waukon Junction on the Mississippi is only about 16 miles off, but the old railroad needed 33 miles to get there, climbing 600 feet through some of the roughest country in Iowa.
